name: Visa and Mastercard debit and credit cards
why: UK Finance: 49.7bn payments in 2025, debit cards more than half of all payments, cards 64% of volume; the base rail Uber and Bolt charge in London.

name: Apple Pay
why: 65% of UK adults registered for a mobile payment service in 2025, up from 57% (UK Finance); Uber UK help and Bolt's card page both list Apple Pay.

name: Worldpay
why: Largest UK acquiring brand; its site cites processing $2.3 trillion annually; no public UK share figure on the site.

name: Google Pay
why: Uber UK help: 'We also accept PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Uber Gift Cards'; Bolt's card page lists GooglePay as not accepted.

name: Barclaycard Payments
why: Barclays' own acquiring arm; 'over 160,000 UK businesses' per its site; no public share figure.

name: Checkout.com
why: Local acquiring in over 50 countries; publishes Uber and FREENOW ride-hailing case studies; $300bn enterprise e-commerce volume in 2025.

name: Adyen
why: EUR 1.4tn processed annually; UK and EU banking licences give local acquiring; Uber shown among its customers.

name: PayPal
why: Uber has offered PayPal to UK riders since Nov 2013 (Great Britain in its first 10 PayPal markets); still on Uber UK help; Bolt UK does not list it.

name: American Express
why: Bolt accepts AMEX cards in app; Uber lets riders pay with American Express reward points; no public Amex share of UK ride payments.

name: Stripe
why: Stripe lists the United Kingdom as a supported country; no public UK share figure.

name: Elavon (U.S. Bank Europe)
why: 'More than two million customers across 36 countries'; UK entity is U.S. Bank Europe DAC; no public UK share figure.

name: Pay by Bank (open banking A2A)
why: OBL: 351M open banking payments in 2025 (+57%), 16.5M user connections; cited use cases are PFM and lending, not ride checkout; Uber and Bolt do not list it.

name: Visa and Mastercard cards (incl. in wallets)
why: Bundesbank 2025: Visa and Mastercard are the most common cards in digital wallets; credit cards 17% of online transactions (2023 diary); Bolt DE accepts Visa and Mastercard.

name: PayPal
why: Bundesbank: e-payment methods 51% of online transactions (2023) and PayPal ~86% of that market (2025); Bolt accepts PayPal only in Germany; Uber DE since 2013.

name: Apple Pay
why: Mobile payments 10% of all German payments in 2025 and Apple Pay the most used mobile method at POS (Bundesbank); Bolt and Uber accept it.

name: Google Pay
why: Germany on Google's online/in-app list; Uber help: riders can pay for trips with Google Pay; Bolt's card page lists GooglePay as not accepted.

name: Payone
why: Self-described 'leading payment service provider in Germany and Austria' (Worldline and Sparkassen joint venture); listed Wero acquirer.

name: Adyen
why: EUR 1.4tn processed annually; EU banking licence gives German local acquiring; Uber shown among its customers.

name: Nexi (formerly Concardis)
why: Nexi Group ranks #1 in European acquiring by merchants and value (~3M merchants, FY2025); German e-commerce business connected to Wero in Apr 2026.

name: Worldline
why: Worldline launched Wero e-commerce acceptance in Germany from summer 2025; German acquiring also via the Payone joint venture.

name: Stripe
why: Stripe lists Germany as a supported country and is a listed Wero acquirer; no public German share figure.

name: Unzer
why: 'Over 90.000 merchants'; DACH methods incl. direct debit, PayPal, Apple Pay and Wero; no public volume figure.

name: girocard
why: ~100M cards and 8.3bn transactions in 2025, but girocard.eu describes POS and in-app functions only; no general e-commerce acceptance stated; no online share figure.

name: SEPA Direct Debit
why: Direct debit plus credit transfer 28% of online transactions (Bundesbank 2023); not listed by Bolt DE; no public ride-hailing evidence.

name: Wero
why: E-commerce live in Germany since 17 Nov 2025 via Sparkassen and VR banks; 46M EU users; acquirers incl. Payone, Nexi, Unzer, Worldline, Stripe, Nuvei, payabl; no mobility use yet.

name: Klarna / Sofort (pay now)
why: Sits in Bundesbank's e-payment bucket where PayPal holds ~86%; Uber DE and Bolt DE help pages do not list Klarna; no public share figure.

name: Visa and Mastercard cards
why: Uber Spain: debit and credit cards accepted; Cabify Spain: Visa, MasterCard, American Express, Diners; Redsys TPV Virtual handles 45M+ payments a month.

name: Apple Pay
why: Uber Spain lists Apple Pay as a card-free option; Redsys TPV Virtual integrates Apple Pay; Spain on Apple's supported list.

name: Redsys (TPV Virtual)
why: Bank-owned national processor; TPV Virtual 'más de 45 millones de pagos al mes'; integrates Bizum, PayPal, Google Pay, Apple Pay; Visa, MC, Amex, JCB, Diners, UnionPay.

name: Comercia Global Payments (CaixaBank)
why: 'Líder en España en servicios de pago para comercios, con un 31,2% de la cuota de mercado por facturación' (Aug 2023); 80% Global Payments, 20% CaixaBank.

name: Google Pay
why: Redsys TPV Virtual integrates Google Pay; Spain on Google's online/in-app list; Uber help: riders can pay for trips with Google Pay.

name: Getnet (Santander)
why: Santander: 'Nuestro adquirente líder en Iberia y Latinoamérica'; Getnet TPV EUR 129bn in 1H26; no Spain-only share figure.

name: Adyen
why: EUR 1.4tn processed annually; EU banking licence gives Spanish local acquiring; Uber shown among its customers.

name: Bizum
why: 31.5M users, 120,000 online merchants, 5.5bn transactions (bizum.com); Redsys gateway integrates it; not listed by Uber, Cabify or Bolt help pages.

name: PayPal
why: Uber Spain and Cabify list PayPal; Cabify recommends it for riders who travel abroad because some banks reject charges from outside the country.

name: Stripe
why: Stripe lists Spain as a supported country; no public Spanish share figure.

name: Checkout.com
why: Local acquiring in over 50 countries across Europe; publishes Uber and FREENOW ride-hailing case studies.

name: Banco Sabadell (Nexi partnership)
why: Sabadell's acquiring runs through a Nexi partnership with Sabadell as Nexi's exclusive distributor in Spain; ~EUR 30M acquiring EBITDA (2023 data).

name: American Express
why: Cabify accepts American Express and Diners; Bolt accepts AMEX in euro-zone countries; no public share figure.

name: Visa and Mastercard credit cards
why: Payments Canada: credit cards 43% of 2025 payment volume and 61% of online shoppers paid by credit card; debit 25%.

name: Apple Pay
why: Canada on Apple's supported list; Uber help: 'you can pay for rides with Apple Pay' once a card is in Wallet.

name: Moneris
why: 'Canada's #1 payment processor', 'more than 325,000 points of commerce', RBC and BMO joint venture.

name: Google Pay
why: Canada on Google's online/in-app list; Uber help: riders can pay for trips with Google Pay.

name: Global Payments Canada
why: #2 Canadian acquirer; bought Desjardins' portfolio of 'approximately 40,000 merchants' (Oct 2019), a leader in Quebec.

name: Adyen
why: EUR 1.4tn processed annually; site cites US, UK and EU licences with no Canada-specific acquiring statement; Uber shown among customers.

name: PayPal
why: Uber added PayPal for Canadian riders in June 2015 (newsroom); still a listed Uber wallet option.

name: Stripe
why: Stripe lists Canada as a supported country; no public Canadian share figure.

name: TD Merchant Solutions
why: 16% share of Canadian acquiring (Speer & Associates, 2012); no newer public figure.

name: Chase Payment Solutions (J.P. Morgan)
why: 8% share of Canadian acquiring (Speer & Associates, 2012); no newer public figure.

name: Interac Debit (online / in-app)
why: 6.6bn Interac Debit transactions in 2024, but Interac describes it as card-present at POS; online route is Interac Direct via Konek; not offered by Uber or Lyft.

name: Elavon Canada
why: 4% share of Canadian acquiring (Speer & Associates, 2012); no newer public figure.

name: Interac e-Transfer
why: 1.4bn transactions in 2024 (Interac); P2P and bill rail, not a ride-hailing checkout method.

name: Debit and credit cards (Visa/Mastercard, dual-network debit)
why: RBA 2025 CPS: debit 49% of payments, credit 23%, online 20% of payments; AP+: debit over 75% of card payments.

name: Apple Pay
why: RBA: device-based payments ~40% of card payments in 2025, up from 31% in 2022; Uber help: pay for rides with Apple Pay.

name: Google Pay
why: Australia on Google's online/in-app list; AP+ 'worked with Google to roll out eftpos functionality and LCR'; Uber help: pay for trips with Google Pay.

name: CommBank merchant services
why: 'Australia's largest financial institution'; standard in-store rate 0.99%; no public acquiring share figure.

name: Adyen
why: EUR 1.4tn processed annually; site cites US, UK and EU licences with no Australia-specific acquiring statement; Uber shown among customers.

name: eftpos (online)
why: On 'over 70 million debit cards'; AP+ cites tokenised e-commerce and LCR with Google; 'Merchant Choice Routing saves nearly 20% on debit'; no public online share.

name: ANZ Worldline Payment Solutions
why: ANZ and Worldline joint venture acquiring under both brands under licence; no public share figure.

name: Westpac (PayWay)
why: Westpac acquiring plus PayWay online gateway; from 1 Oct 2026 rates 0.79% EFTPOS/PayWay and 1.25% OnlinePay; no public share figure.

name: Stripe
why: Stripe lists Australia as a supported country; no public Australian share figure.

name: PayPal
why: Australia among Uber's first PayPal markets (Nov 2013); no current Australia-specific Uber help page found; no public share figure.

name: NAB merchant services
why: Big-4 bank acquirer; its merchant page gives no merchant count or share figure.

name: Tyro
why: 'Fifth largest merchant acquiring bank in Australia', over 73,000 merchants (RBA submission 2025); SMB and in-store focus.

name: PayTo
why: NPP mandate rail; 'Amazon Australia now offers PayTo at checkout' (Jun 2025); RBA: 4pp of A2A payments in 2025; no ride-hailing acceptance found.

name: Fat Zebra
why: Australian gateway; AsiaPay partnership to 'accelerate our growth in Australia and New Zealand'; no public volume figure.

name: Visa and Mastercard cards (scheme debit and credit)
why: Payments NZ: credit cards usable 'in store, online or overseas', only 'some debit cards' online, EFTPOS cards not; the online card rail for rides.

name: Apple Pay
why: Payments NZ 2026: 25% prefer smartphones for everyday purchases, up from 15% in 2024; NZ on Apple's list; Uber help: pay rides with Apple Pay.

name: Google Pay
why: New Zealand on Google's online/in-app list; Uber help: riders can pay for trips with Google Pay.

name: Worldline NZ (Paymark)
why: National switch 'for more than 35 years', 'millions of everyday transactions'; no public share figure on its site.

name: Windcave
why: NZ-headquartered gateway serving 'thousands of the world's most recognizable brands'; owner of Account2Account; no public volume figure.

name: Stripe
why: Stripe lists New Zealand as a supported country; no public NZ share figure.

name: Adyen
why: EUR 1.4tn processed annually; site cites US, UK and EU licences with no NZ-specific acquiring statement; Uber shown among customers.

name: PayPal
why: Uber added PayPal for New Zealand riders in June 2015 (newsroom); no public NZ share figure.

name: Account2Account (Windcave)
why: Real-time online bank transfer with ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Kiwibank, Co-operative Bank, TSB and Westpac; no ride-hailing acceptance found.

name: Open banking payments (API Centre standards)
why: '180,000 open banking payments in Aotearoa last month' (API Centre headline); API Centre ceased operating 30 Sep 2026 as standards moved to a next phase.

name: EFTPOS (domestic debit)
why: Payments NZ describes EFTPOS cards as withdraw or deposit at terminals, no online use stated; not usable for in-app rides.

name: POLi
why: Still offered in NZ as of May 2024 but ASB, BNZ and Westpac say use breaches their T&Cs (Consumer NZ); Australian arm closed Sept 2023.
